topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, housekeeping, and learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Tumor virology, cellular oncogenes, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the history of tumor virology and explain how studying viral oncogenes and transformation assays revealed that cancer originates from altered cellular genes.

topics.label: Classification and mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the functional classifications of cancer-driving mutations and illustrate how oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes operate through cell cycle regulation and allele dosage effects.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the distinctions between sequence and chromosomal instability, detailing the DNA repair failures, replication errors, and mitotic defects that generate them and their cellular outcomes.

topics.label: Multistep tumor progression and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how sequential mutation accumulation and inherited genetic predispositions accelerate the development of cancer.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing, recommended reading, and concluding remarks for the lecture.
